critiques.issue: The tip rests on one run with a +0.21 pp margin. The notebook puts the per-trial sd from nondeterminism at 0.3-0.4 pp (same seed, up to 0.9 pp apart), so the 3-seed-mean sd is about 0.2 pp and E031 sits only about 1 sd above 0.753. Seed 1 came in at 75.13. The loop's own H1.1.3 rule (margin < 0.3 pp means rerun and pool) fired in the E031 notebook entry, but E032-E035 were all stacked on E031 without that rerun. H1.1.3, the noise-floor measurement that every verdict since E023 depends on, has never been run either.
critiques.suggestion: Before anything else, rerun E031 unchanged twice and E028 once. Pool the results to get the noise floor (sd of a 3-seed mean and sd of a run-to-run difference). If pooled E031 drops below 0.7535, revert the tip to E028 and re-judge E033-E035 against the pooled baseline.

critiques.target: E034 verdict / I047 rationale (resize vs epochs under Muon)
critiques.issue: Units were mixed up. I047 says 'under Muon, epochs cost ~0.31 pp/s (E027)', but 0.31 is pp per epoch. In seconds, E031's epoch cut cost 0.23 pp for 0.41 s, about 0.56 pp/s. E034's resize rate is 0.18 pp / 0.24 s = 0.75 pp/s, and with a difference sd of about 0.3 pp its error bar is roughly ±1.2 pp/s. So '0.75 > 0.45 → resize costs more than epochs' compares 0.75±1.2 with 0.56±0.7. That is no evidence either way. The projected '40% @ 8.0 ep → 5.2 s' frontier rests on this.
critiques.suggestion: Mark E034 inconclusive. Measure the two rates head-to-head over larger spans (e.g. 30% vs 50% at 24 px, and 8.0 vs 9.5 ep), with replicated endpoints so each rate's error is under ±0.3 pp/s.

critiques.target: H1.2 / H5.2 (block-3 width is binding), E013 vs E021
critiques.issue: The descriptions disagree on the translate setting in this lineage. E017 says E013 used translate 4, while E021 says E013 (commit b0eba3b) used translate 2. E018/E019 say E012 used translate 4, while E020 says translate 2. If E013 had translate 4 and E021 had translate 2, E021's +0.33 pp, the only evidence for 'block 3 is binding', is fully confounded with translate 4→2 (worth +0.35 pp in E011). Even without the confound, +0.33 pp is about 1 sd of a difference, and E013 had a wide seed spread (74.61-75.74).
critiques.suggestion: Diff commits b0eba3b, 6d40ead and 12fffd2 for translate amplitude. Then re-test block 3 at 576 vs 704 vs 896 on the current Muon tip with replication. Set H1.2 and H5.2 confidence according to the result.

critiques.target: Lvl1 coverage: optimizer geometry and weight averaging
critiques.issue: None of the Lvl1s explains the three biggest recent effects: Muon +0.78 pp (E025), removing Lookahead −0.81 pp (E035), and batch 3072 −1.04 pp under Muon while 1024→2048 was flat (E032). H4 frames these as 'mis-tuned 37-epoch constants', and H1 is still written around SGD-era lever rates and the 6.65 s E023 tip. The current story has no account of why averaging matters more under Muon, or why step count becomes binding below ~200 steps.
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl1 along the lines of 'update geometry + iterate averaging set sample efficiency: Muon's fixed-norm steps make step count and averaging first-order'. Give it falsifiable children: Lookahead k/alpha sweep, EMA tail, Muon momentum, NS iterations, Muon lr vs batch. Refresh H1's numbers to the Muon tip.

critiques.target: H4.4 (sample-limited, batch as pure throughput lever)
critiques.issue: E032 contradicts the H4.4 statement under Muon, yet H4.4 stays open with its unconditional wording. E032's explanation ('Muon movement is per step') was not tested by E033, which raised Muon lr at batch 2048, not 3072. E032 also has untested confounds. The Lookahead sync count is tied to steps (E035 shows Lookahead is first-order), warmup is a fixed fraction of fewer steps, and dropping the last partial batch at 3072 discards 856 images per epoch (about 1.7%). H4.4.2 (batch 1536 on E023) was already answered by E024 but is still open.
critiques.suggestion: Restate H4.4 as SGD-only and close H4.4.2. If the batch axis is reopened, run 3072 with the Lookahead cadence held fixed in examples (not steps) before any Muon lr scaling, to separate averaging from step size.

critiques.issue: The E035 post-mortem says the LR ends at 7% of peak, not 0. H4 and H4.5 say the schedule decays to 0, and H4.5.1 proposes a 5% floor 'instead of 0'. Either the post-mortem or the hypotheses describe the code wrongly, and H4.5.1's prediction is meaningless until that is settled.
critiques.suggestion: Read the LR table in the tip commit. Then rewrite H4.5.1 against the actual schedule, e.g. a floor of 0 vs 7% vs 15%, combined with an EMA tail.

critiques.issue: H3 and H3.2 still claim a steady ~0.4 pp/s resize cost proportional to FLOPs removed. E029 (1.8 pp/s at 75%) shows a threshold, and E034 (if it means anything) shows a different rate under Muon. E034 is still logged as E034+ under H3.2, even though its rate contradicts H3.2's stated 0.4 pp/s. H3.2.5 carries E029- but is marked 'open' rather than refuted.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H3.2.5 refuted. Rewrite H3.2 as 'resize rate is optimizer-dependent and nonlinear above ~50%; ≥ ~4-5 epochs at 32 px needed'. Change E034 to ~ under H3.2.

critiques.issue: The post-mortem blames too little high-LR time at 32 px. That is plausible but untested, and other explanations fit too. BN running statistics may be dominated by 24 px batches if momentum is low. Translate was not scaled to 24 px. Muon's orthogonalized updates on 4x4/6x6 block-3 maps during the long low-res phase may also distort the filters.
critiques.suggestion: Run one cheap discriminating test at 75% low-res: put the 32 px phase in the middle of the run, or reset BN stats with a short 32 px recalibration inside train. Either recovers accuracy if mismatch is the cause, not reduced FLOPs.

critiques.target: Single-run verdicts within noise (E005, E011, E014, E017, E033, E028)
critiques.issue: Several tree claims rest on single differences of 0.1-0.4 pp, which is within 1-1.5 sd of a run-to-run difference. These include alternating flip helps (−0.41), translate 2 helps (+0.35), LS 0 hurts (−0.31), concave epoch curve (E017 +0.11 pp/ep), Muon lr optimum ≤0.24 (−0.33) and batch 2048 is free (−0.11). E020's '0.52 pp/ep' slope is likewise a 2-run difference. H1's lever rates have stated errors (±0.2-0.3 pp/s) about as large as the gaps between the rates being ranked.
critiques.suggestion: Once the noise floor is measured, relabel these as inconclusive where |Δ| < 2·sd(diff). Rerun only those that a pending decision depends on (translate under Muon, Muon lr, batch 2048).

critiques.target: Untried directions with high expected value
critiques.issue: Several cheap options were never run: a profile of the Muon tip (H2.4.3; Muon alone is ~1.66 ms of a ~25 ms step, and NS iteration count is a direct cost lever); whole-run CUDA graph (H2.4.4); Lookahead alpha/k tuning or an EMA tail (pointed to by E035); translate 1/0 under Muon (pointed to by E030, −0.62 pp for 2→4); Muon momentum (0.6 is a CIFAR-10 setting) and lr 0.2; whiten_bias_epochs (H4.5.2); block-3 896 and block-2 192 under Muon (H1.2.4/H1.2.5); head feature-dimension tests (H5.2.x); depth per block (H1.2.3).
critiques.suggestion: After the E031 replication, prioritize: (1) profile, then cut NS iterations from 5 to 3 or fewer and fuse the elementwise kernels; (2) Lookahead/EMA sweep as a margin source; (3) translate 1 under Muon. Spend any margin gained on epochs.

critiques.issue: Several open nodes are framed on obsolete SGD bases (E004, E023) or describe levers that are already closed: H5.1.1 on the E004 base, H1.2.3/H1.2.4/H5.2.x on E023, and H2 still sized as '1-2 ms of a ~9-14 ms step'. Results from those bases would not carry over to the Muon/bs2048/8.75-ep tip, since E030/E032/E035 show the interactions change sign or size under Muon.

structured_output.summary: The current tip, E031 at 5.43 s, rests on one run with a +0.21 pp margin, about 1 sd of a 3-seed mean. Its own rerun rule fired and was skipped, and E032-E035 were judged against it. The noise-floor measurement (H1.1.3) was never run, so many verdicts rest on single differences of 0.1-0.4 pp that are within noise: alternating flip, translate 2, LS 0, Muon lr, batch 2048 being free, and the concave epoch curve. The E034 conclusion that resize costs more than epochs under Muon comes from a unit mix-up (0.31 pp/epoch read as pp/s; the real epoch rate is ~0.56 pp/s) and a +0.18 pp difference, so it is noise. The descriptions contradict each other on the translate setting and on which base each experiment used. If E013 had translate 4, E021's +0.33 pp, the only evidence that block 3 is binding (H1.2/H5.2), is confounded with the translate change. The tree is also out of date with the results. H4.2 still predicts Muon loses, though it gave +0.78 pp and is now the backbone. H4.4's 'batch is free' claim is contradicted under Muon by E032. H3/H3.2 still claim a linear ~0.4 pp/s resize cost despite E029's threshold. H3.2.5 is not marked refuted. The E035 post-mortem's 7% LR floor contradicts H4/H4.5.1's 'decay to 0'. No Lvl1 explains the three biggest recent effects: Muon's gain, the large cost of removing Lookahead, and Muon's sensitivity to step count. A Lvl1 on update geometry plus iterate averaging is missing. Cheap directions never tried: profile the Muon tip and cut Newton-Schulz iterations, a whole-run CUDA graph, tuning Lookahead or adding an EMA tail, translate 1 under Muon, Muon momentum, whiten_bias_epochs, and block-width changes under Muon. Order of work: replicate E031 and E028, fix the base-lineage records, then use those levers to build margin and spend it on epochs.
